evidence: `body = source.split(":", 1)[1]  # drop the def line so params are not counted as reads`
`assert body.count(name) > 1, ( ... "is declared but never read in transition_core's body" ... )`

The diff's own txn.py comment block names `force_close_reason` in prose (line 289-296), so a comment reference — not an actual read — would satisfy `count(name) > 1`; the assertion does not truly verify the parameter is used.

advisory.finding: AC4 test asserts on the source text of the unit under test (inspect.getsource + substring count) rather than its behavior — a source-grepping change-detector that breaks on a behavior-preserving refactor and can be satisfied by a mere comment mention.
scenarios: A future refactor that keeps force_close_reason on the event but reads it under a different local name or via a helper breaks this test with no behavior change.
A comment mentioning the parameter name inflates the count and lets a genuinely-unread parameter pass.
